title: A rename carries over to open purchase order lines at every location
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin who can switch between two locations: the test location and location B.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test at the test location, with 4 on hand, and at location B under the same part number.
  • Create an open purchase order for this test at the test location, purchase order 1, from any vendor, with a line for part A picked from the lookup, 2 ordered and none received.
  • Create an open purchase order for this test at location B, purchase order 2, from any vendor, with a line for part A picked from the lookup, 4 ordered and none received.
  • Use a new part number that no part and no Part Library entry has yet, and that does not contain part A's number.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Replace the Part Number with the new number.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  6. Open purchase order 1.
  7. Pick location B in the location selector at the top right.
  8. Click Parts in the top bar.
  9. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  10. Open purchase order 2.
  11. Pick the test location in the location selector at the top right.
  12. Click Parts in the top bar.
  13. Click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  14. Open purchase order 1.
  15. Click Receive.
  16. Type an invoice number in the invoice number field.
  17. Type 10.00 as the cost.
  18. Type 20.00 as the sell price.
  19. Type 2 as the received quantity.
  20. Click Receive on the Receive screen.
  21. Click Inventory in the left menu.
  22. Type the new number in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed with 4 on hand.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Part Number shows the new number.

Step 4:

  • The rename is saved and the window closes.

Step 5:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 6:

  • Purchase order 1's open line now reads the new number.

Step 7:

  • The location selector shows location B.

Step 8:

  • The Parts left menu shows Purchase Orders.

Step 9:

  • Location B's Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 10:

  • Purchase order 2's open line at location B reads the new number: the rename reaches every location.

Step 11:

  • The location selector shows the test location.

Step 12:

  • The Parts left menu shows Purchase Orders.

Step 13:

  • The Purchase Orders list opens.

Step 14:

  • Purchase order 1 opens with its line under the new number.

Step 15:

  • The Receive screen opens, with the line under the new number.

Step 16:

  • The invoice number shows what you typed.

Step 17:

  • The cost shows 10.00.

Step 18:

  • The sell price shows 20.00.

Step 19:

  • The received quantity shows 2.

Step 20:

  • Receiving finds the renamed part and the delivery is accepted.

Step 21:

  • The Inventory page opens.

Step 22:

  • Part A is listed under the new number with 6 Available (4 + 2 = 6).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S13-R19: “A rename carries over to open work that holds this part, at every location: purchase order lines not yet fully received, part requests not yet received or returned, canned jobs, and returns that are not completed take the new number. A delivery that is not yet accepted is covered by its open purchase order lines. Receiving, ordering, applying a canned job and returning then find the renamed part.”
  • Key Decisions: “A rename carries over to work that is still open. Open purchase order lines, open part requests, canned jobs and open returns follow the new number, so receiving and returning still find the part. Records already completed keep the number they were written with.”
  • Terminology: “Open work → A purchase order line not yet fully received, a part request not yet received or returned, a canned job, and a return that is not completed.”
